sections.h2: Who to call about a Grayson County tax bill
sections.html:
Three offices touch a Grayson County property tax bill, and each holds a different piece. The sheriff collects current bills at 117 S. Main Street in Leitchfield, KY 42754, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Central Time, phone (270) 259-3024. Values and exemption forms come from the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) at (270) 259-4838. Once a real property bill is transferred, the Grayson County Clerk at (270) 259-5295 quotes the payoff.

A buyer's title company will want to know which office holds each tax year, so have all three numbers handy before you list.

  • The sheriff accepts payment on the online portal, through the mail or over the counter. Cards work in both places, with a processing fee.
  • The sheriff takes the full bill only. There are no installments and no partial payments.
  • A bill that has not shown up by November 10 can be replaced. Call the sheriff with the address and owner name.
  • If a lender escrows your taxes, hand the bill over and check later that the payment actually went out.

The sheriff's 2026 schedule runs the discount from November 1 through November 30. The face amount is due during December, and penalties start in 2027. Kentucky's statewide default under KRS 134.015 ends the discount on November 1, so follow the dates the sheriff publishes instead.

sections.h2: Fire and rescue dues on the bill
sections.html:
Many bills carry a membership charge for the county's fire districts. An owner can skip it for a single year by signing an opt-out form and sending it in with the payment. The sheriff asks people who plan to opt out to phone before paying online.

The form has a warning that matters when a house is for sale or sitting empty. Under KRS 75.450, an owner who opts out can be billed by the fire district for at least $500 or $1,000, depending on the type of facility, after a fire or other non-medical incident at the property. The form must be renewed every year.

If you are listing, decide on the dues before you pay and tell the closing agent which way you went.

Start with a conference at the Grayson County PVA, because Kentucky bars an owner from the local board without one. Call (270) 259-4838. The assessment roll sits open for viewing for 13 days, counting from the first Monday in May.

  • At the conference the PVA explains how the number was built and records your claimed value and any change you both accept.
  • Once the viewing period ends, you have until the following business day to lodge the appeal with the county clerk.
  • A local board hears cases about four to five weeks afterward. Bring repair estimates, insurance records, photos and listings of nearby sales. An appeal with no paper behind it gets denied.
  • Skip the hearing and you lose the later route to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Anyone you pay to speak for you must come from the state's approved professions, such as attorneys, CPAs and appraisers, and needs your written authority. If bills were already printed and the board sets a value above your claim, the clerk sends a supplemental bill for the difference.

The exemption belongs to Grayson homeowners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and applies only to their own residence. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years the state sets it at $49,100 off the assessed value.

Take a birth certificate, license or passport to the PVA as proof of age. A disability claim needs different papers, so ask the PVA what qualifies and how often the claim must be renewed.

After a sale, ask the PVA what to file so the exemption comes off the house you sold and can be claimed on your next home.

Unpaid tax follows the land, and a buyer's title search will surface it. The owner on January 1 carries the debt, and KRS 134.420 lets the lien on a delinquent bill last 11 years through any change of ownership.

Once a bill is at the clerk, it grows by 1 percent a month plus commissions. Notices from the county attorney go out around day 30 and day 60. A certificate sale may follow 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and whoever buys at it can tack on more.

Before you list, get two payoff figures: this year's from the sheriff and any transferred bills from the clerk. The closing agent can pay both from the sale price. A cash buyer who closes fast can often clear these the same week, which matters if the clerk's sale date is close.

A short checklist saves time at closing. Find your latest bill, or ask the sheriff for a copy. Confirm with the sheriff whether this year's bill is paid and ask the clerk whether any older year has been transferred. If you have an exemption on the house, tell the PVA you are selling. If you opted out of fire dues, tell the closing agent so the settlement statement matches what you actually paid.

Title companies split the current year's bill between buyer and seller at the table, so know which window you are in before you set a closing date. Closing in the discount window gives the buyer a lower bill to share. Closing after April 15 means the bill is probably at the clerk and the payoff will be higher.

Leitchfield is both the seat and the largest city of this rural west central Kentucky county. Residents numbered 27,406 in July 2025, a 3.7 percent gain over April 2020. The 2020 census counted 13,275 housing units, 21.4 percent of them vacant. Owners occupy 74.6 percent of housing. The median home is valued at $164,600, and owners pay $1,274 monthly with a mortgage or $416 without. Two Army Corps of Engineers lakes, Rough River Lake and Nolin River Lake, shape the local market.

Someone dealing with a roof leak, a cracked foundation or a lien can sell a Grayson County house as is to a cash buyer, which skips repair negotiations and lender appraisals.

faqs.q: When does the 2026 discount end in Grayson County?
faqs.a: On November 30, 2026. The sheriff's schedule starts the discount on November 1, then shows the face amount for December and a 5 percent penalty in January 2027.

faqs.q: Does the Grayson County Sheriff accept installments?
faqs.a: No. The office wants the whole bill at once and refuses partial payments. If a lender escrows your taxes, it can send the full amount for you.

faqs.q: My Grayson County bill never came. What now?
faqs.a: Phone the sheriff at (270) 259-3024 after November 10 and ask for a duplicate. Give the property address and the owner's name.

faqs.q: Where do I settle a Grayson County bill after April 15?
faqs.a: With the County Clerk at (270) 259-5295. Real property bills still open on that date move to the clerk, who quotes the payoff including interest and commissions.

faqs.q: Who takes homestead applications in Grayson County?
faqs.a: The PVA, at (270) 259-4838. Bring proof of age or disability. The 2025 and 2026 exemption takes $49,100 off assessed value.
